chapter: Cliff Jackson, Jelly Roll Morton and Harlem in the 1920s
title: The Nest Club and Harlem's Seventh Avenue clubs
summary: The Nest was off Seventh Avenue at 133rd Street amid Tillie's Chicken Shack, Small's and other clubs.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, how big a place was the Nest?

It was located on 100 -- just off Seventh Avenue and 133rd Street. Well, that particular street, there are so many different clubs in there, like Tillie's Chicken Shack and all them different places. You know, people from downtown would come up there, Paradise giblet, 135th and Seventh. Harlem was the place where everybody would come.
Well, Small's was bigger than the Nest, wasn't it?
Oh, yes, Small's was still there on 135th Street.
Yeah. But where you went upstairs, and down, you would play. Most -- that time we were downstairs.
